properties.name: Per-item lineage holds through a conflict resolved mid-merge, a re-export repairs a stale prev, and compare reads a checksum on the node and on its change as one design
properties.rationale: The lineage is the anchor's to state, not the file's: an export is the act that writes it, so an export must be able to put it right. #571's fourth CI failure (an export mid-merge chaining from the older main) is the case ver:item-lineage-survives-squash-merge-and-a-mid-merge-export was written to reproduce; its test's mid-merge export only wrote a NEW item, which has no predecessor, so it passed without exercising the case. The new test resolves a both-sides conflict during the merge, exactly as AGENTS.md tells a contributor to, and was seen failing on the pre-fix binary. Same class for compare: a derived value the export elides must be derived back by every reader of a document, not only by the import.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Review of #672 (fix program item 13, step 2) found three defects in the item layout, each reproduced on the real binary before the fix. (1) A real conflict resolved DURING a merge of main mis-chained: with HEAD still the branch's own tip, the export anchored at merge-base(HEAD, main) from before the merge, so the resolved item named the version main had already replaced; the gate failed LINEAGE on the merge commit and no re-export could repair it, because the item's content no longer moved. Now the anchor is the merge-base of main with HEAD and MERGE_HEAD together while a merge is in progress (what the gate asks once it is committed), and every write re-checks the lineage of the items that already differ from the anchor and relinks a stale prev (item_layout::plan_write_rechecking; receipt items.relinked). (2) The gate read `git diff --name-only` without -z, so a path git quotes (any byte past ASCII, which an escaped id passes through) dropped out of LINEAGE and coverage; now -z in Rust and Python. (3) compare_designs read the checksum move as 541 changed artifacts across reflow2's own conversion, though no checksum moved; both sides are now read with the import's rule (export::fill_accepted_checksum). Also an interrupted item write now leaves a hidden temporary file every reader skips.
